text:
Marathon Petroleum fell 1.8% today after surging 8% yesterday on the Trump-Putin diesel deal announcement. The reversal suggests investors are reassessing the agreement's actual benefits to U.S. refiners—importing Russian diesel directly competes with domestic refinery output, potentially undercutting prices and margins even as crude oil prices remain elevated at $96/barrel domestically and $125 globally. With U.S. refineries already running at 92.7% capacity and facing hurricane disruptions in the Gulf of Mexico, cheaper imported fuel could crimp profitability despite tight fuel stocks.

The stock's 15.6% gain over two weeks reflects the volatile backdrop: Middle East tensions pushed oil higher, but the diesel import deal signals the Trump administration may prioritize lower consumer fuel prices over supporting domestic refiner margins. For a refiner, that's a mixed signal at best.
